facts.statement: Propanoplosaurus was a herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Patuxent Formation of Maryland, USA.
facts.quote: Propanoplosaurus is a genus of herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Patuxent Formation of Maryland, USA.

facts.statement: The species Propanoplosaurus marylandicus was named and described by Stanford, Weishampel, and DeLeon in 2011.
facts.quote: The type species, Propanoplosaurus marylandicus was named and described by Stanford, David Weishampel, and Valerie DeLeon in 2011.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen USNM 540686 was found in the Patuxent Formation, which dates to the late Aptian.
facts.quote: The holotype, USNM 540686, was found in the Patuxent Formation, dating from the late Aptian.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the specimen is thirteen centimetres.
facts.quote: The specimen has a preserved length of thirteen centimetres.

facts.statement: The total estimated length of the individual was between twenty-four and twenty-eight centimetres.
facts.quote: The total length of the individual was estimated at between twenty-four and twenty-eight centimetres.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that osteoderms appearing only on the skull and a long snout with a unique cross-pattern of bone plates were common developmental stages in nodosaurids.
facts.quote: Only the skull shows osteoderms, and the authors suggest this was a common developmental stage of all nodosaurids, together with a long middle section of the snout, which is characterised by a unique cross-pattern of the bone plates, probably formed by the triangular osteoderms of the maxillae.

facts.statement: The describers assigned Propanoplosaurus to the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Propanoplosaurus was by the describers assigned to the Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Propanoplosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian stage, approximately 112 million years ago in North America.
facts.quote: Propanoplosaurus marylandicus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Propanoplosaurus de dinosaurio tireóforo nodosáurido que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, durante el Aptiense, hace aproximadamente 112 millones de años, en Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Propanoplosaurus is from 119.57 to 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The fossil specimen is preserved showing the animal lying on its back.
facts.quote: The animal is shown lying on its back.

rejected.quote: Along with dinosaur footprints, the impressions of a neonate nodosaurid, specimen USNM 540686, were found by Stanford in 1997.
